pr_title: Remove CPU-specific info from cpuidle dimensions
pr_body:
##### Summary
In order to fix chart aggregation on Netdata Cloud, we remove the CPU-specific info from dimension names for cpuidle charts. We also provide more meaningful context for the charts.

Fixes #12889

##### Test Plan
Make API request `http://localhost:19999/api/v1/chart?chart=cpu.cpu0_cpuidle`. It should show the new context name and dimension names in the response
```
"context": "cpuidle.cpu_cstate_residency_time",

"dimensions": {
	"active": { "name": "C0 (active)" },
	"poll": { "name": "POLL" },
	"c1": { "name": "C1" }
},
```

issue_context.title: [Bug]: cpuidle charts dimension  ids contain instance specific info, it should be removed
issue_context.body: ### Bug description Because it "breaks" the charts' aggregation on the Overview page on Netdata Cloud. ### Expected behavior ```json "dimensions": { "cpu0_active_time": { "name": "C0 (active)" }, "cpu0_cpuidle_state0_time": { "name": "POLL" }, "cpu0_cpuidle_state1_time": { "name": "C1_ACPI" }, "cpu0_cpuidle_state2_time": { "name": "C2_ACPI" }, "cpu0_cpuidle_state3_time": { "name": "C3_ACPI" } }, ``` I think we can just use state (lowercase) names ```json "dimensions": { "active": { "name": "C0 (active)" }, "poll": { "name": "POLL" }, "c1_acpi": { "name": "C1_ACPI" }, "c2_acpi": { "name": "C2_ACPI" }, "c3_acpi": { "name": "C3_ACPI" } }, ``` --- In addition I think we need to change the context: `cpuidle.cpuidle` => `cpuidle.cpu_cstate_residency_time` (or something like that, `cpuidle.cpuidle` is wrong). ### Steps to reproduce - 448 different dimensions. - a lot of duplicate states. ### Installation method kickstart.sh ### System info ```shell n/a ``` ### Netdata build info ```shell netdata v1.34.0-155-g73bb8888f ``` ### Additional info _No response_

review_comments: Should we sanitize the value in addition to tolower here? It is possible a state name can have spaces or ()?
No names with whitespaces or parentheses in the kernel. Only `_` and `-`.

Perhaps we can make it a function, e.g. `strtolower` and put in https://github.com/netdata/netdata/tree/master/libnetdata/string, I see we do the same in https://github.com/netdata/netdata/blob/de5ed03f8a8cd6abf39d364f352ab1f3c3f928c0/daemon/global_statistics.c#L1290=
